articles.title: 谷歌发布 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 模型：主打日常编程与智能体工作流，百万 Token 输入 1.5 美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，谷歌正式推出 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 模型，主打快速执行与高效运行，面向日常编码和智能体工作流场景，将 Gemini 4 系列能力全面下放至所有层级用户。输入：每百万 Tokens 1.50 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 10.0 元人民币）输出：每百万 Tokens 7.50 美元（现汇率约合 50.1 元人民币）该定价覆盖全 100 万 Token 上下文窗口，无分段阶梯计价。在 Artificial Analysis 智能指数中，Hydrogen 默认高思考档位得分 51，高于 Gemini 4 Argon 的 50，最高 xhigh 档位可达 54，同时任务完成速度常优于同级别模型。谷歌同步推出 Orchestrator 智能调度功能，内置于 Google Antigravity 平台，可在同一会话中自动在 Carbon 与 Hydrogen 等模型间动态切换。在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 测试中，该调度方案达到接近 Carbon 的任务成功率，同时平均消耗配额减少 24%，完成速度提升 19%。对比上一代 Gemini 3.8 Flash，Hydrogen 默认高思考档位下任务完成速度提升 2.5 倍，Terminal-Bench 4.1 得分从 18.2% 提升至 57%，虚构错误率降低 5 倍以上。该模型设置四档思考深度：low、medium、high（默认）、xhigh，可根据任务需求灵活调节推理深度、延迟与成本；支持最高 100 万 Token 原生输入、100 万 Token 输出，可处理大型 PDF、表格、图表、音视频等多模态内容。安全方面，Hydrogen 将智能体任务越权行为减少最高 81%，服务不足问题减少 79%，工具调用与编码场景下的失准行为、任务走捷径问题减少 12 倍；内部智能体诚实度评测得分 96.7%，思维链保留率达 99.9%，在 Gray Swan IPI 基准上对抗间接提示注入的韧性提升 2.3 倍以上。从发布当日起，Hydrogen 全球范围陆续开放：开发者可通过 Gemini API、AI Studio、Android Studio 付费层调用；企业可通过 Gemini for 商业版、Google Antigravity、表格内 Gemini 部署；普通用户可在 Gemini 应用下拉选择模型，免费用户在自动模型选择模式下也可获得适配的 Hydrogen 能力，同时谷歌搜索也同步接入该模型升级体验。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，2027 年是《星球大战》系列诞生 50 周年，阿斯顿 · 马丁宣布与迪士尼、卢卡斯影业合作，共同庆祝这一里程碑。阿斯顿 · 马丁计划在未来一年举办系列活动，回顾《星球大战》的发展历程，但具体内容尚未公布。阿斯顿 · 马丁透露，双方将通过周年庆期间的一系列活动及合作项目，展现英国顶级奢华工艺与电影叙事的艺术魅力。阿斯顿 · 马丁全球营销总监芬巴尔 · 麦克福尔表示：“过去 50 年，《星球大战》证明了设计与叙事能够产生非凡的力量，激励世界各地一代又一代人。阿斯顿 · 马丁同样致力于打造个性鲜明、能够引发长久情感共鸣的产品和体验，因此双方的合作顺理成章，也令人期待。”据IT之家了解，阿斯顿 · 马丁旗下产品从未在《星球大战》电影中亮相。相比之下，阿斯顿 · 马丁与《007》系列电影的渊源更深。不过，阿斯顿 · 马丁与《星球大战》并非毫无联系。2024 年 3 月，阿斯顿 · 马丁申请注册了 Venator 商标，而《星球大战》中的银河共和国恰好也拥有名为 Venator 的狩猎者级歼星舰。阿斯顿 · 马丁计划在 2027 年初公布更多周年庆活动安排。除了与迪士尼、卢卡斯影业联合举办活动，阿斯顿 · 马丁有望借机推出以太空为主题的特别版车型或配置套件。今年 7 月，面临持续资金压力的阿斯顿 · 马丁获得了约 7.35 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 49.14 亿元人民币）的新债务融资，并称这笔资金将用于支持后续产品计划。

articles.title: 黄仁勋辞任英伟达 CEO 重创全球 AI 概念股，AMD、博通逆势上涨
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，据路透社报道，黄仁勋因婚外情丑闻持续发酵而辞去英伟达 CEO，引发全球 AI 概念股周四大跌。英伟达领导层突遭变动，也让原本就面临融资和监管压力的 AI 行业增添了新的风险。英伟达宣布，CFO 科莱特 · 克雷斯将暂任 CEO，公司同时寻找正式接班人。作为 AI 产业链的核心企业，英伟达不仅供应芯片，还为采用其芯片的数据中心等基础设施项目提供资金支持，这种商业模式因循环融资问题受到质疑。随着英伟达陷入更深的危机，整个 AI 行业也面临新的压力。英伟达股价早盘下跌 8.2%，跌至 16 个多月以来的最低水平，市值更是 2025 年 7 月以来首次跌破 4 万亿美元。英伟达投资的新型云计算服务商 CoreWeave 股价下跌 9.1%。就在前一个交易日，CoreWeave 还因财报表现带动 AI 概念股反弹，单日涨幅超过 27%。其他新型云计算服务商也未能幸免，IREN 和 Applied Digital 股价双双走低。Nebius 则在宣布 2026 年营收将接近此前预测区间下限后，股价大跌 16.2%。自英伟达董事会周日宣布调查黄仁勋的婚外情丑闻以来，公司市值蒸发超过 5,500 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 3.68 万亿元人民币）。盈透证券首席市场分析师史蒂夫 · 索斯尼克指出：“英伟达与行业内众多企业之间存在盘根错节的交易关系。究竟让整个行业更加稳定，还是更加脆弱？随着事态在未来几周逐渐明朗，答案也会浮出水面。”数据分析公司 ORTEX 的数据显示，仅本周以来，做空英伟达的投资者就获得了 96 亿美元（现汇率约合 641.84 亿元人民币）的账面收益。芯片制造商一直被视为 AI 热潮的主要受益者，此次也成为抛售潮的重灾区，费城半导体指数下跌 1.3%。美满电子股价下跌 3.8%。黄仁勋今年 6 月曾点名美满电子，称其有望成为“下一家万亿美元公司”。甲骨文也下跌 2.6%，公司正扩大与英伟达在云端 AI 芯片方面的合作。其他科技股同样承压。美光科技下跌 2.5%，闪迪和西部数据分别下跌 6% 和 3.7%。光子器件制造商 Lumentum、Coherent，以及 AI 服务器制造商戴尔的跌幅在 3% 至 5.1% 之间。建筑及发电设备制造商卡特彼勒和电力企业 Vistra 则分别下跌约 0.5%。与英伟达竞争的另外两家 AI 芯片制造商 AMD 和博通逆势上涨，涨幅分别为 3.7% 和 5.6%。投资者预期，英伟达陷入动荡可能为竞争对手创造机会。Alphabet、亚马逊和微软等大型云服务商的股价也上涨了 0.8% 至 2.7%。全球科技股市场同样出现震荡。日本和韩国股市均收跌近 0.7%，欧洲科技股也下跌约 1%。伦敦证券交易所集团汇总的数据显示，英伟达目前的未来 12 个月预期市盈率约为 12 倍，降至 2012 年 11 月以来的最低水平。

articles.title: 欧几里得望远镜公布首批大规模观测数据：涵盖超 9 亿个星系
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，欧洲航天局（ESA）公布了欧几里得（Euclid）空间望远镜任务首批大规模观测数据。这项任务旨在绘制宇宙的大尺度结构，此次公布的数据涵盖了超过 9 亿个星系的观测结果。科学家希望借此进一步研究宇宙中两种至今仍充满谜团的成分：暗物质和暗能量。当地时间周四公布的数据覆盖了相当于从地球上看到的月球视面积约 9500 倍的天空区域。欧几里得望远镜的最终目标是在 2031 年前绘制有史以来规模最大的宇宙三维地图，覆盖整个天空三分之一以上的区域。此次发布的数据来自欧几里得望远镜约 13 个月的观测，数据总量高达 1.7 PB（拍字节），相当于 170 万 GB。欧洲航天局欧几里得项目科学家、天体物理学家瓦莱里娅 · 佩托里诺（Valeria Pettorino）表示：“这对欧洲航天局的欧几里得任务以及所有参与其中的人员来说，都是一个重要的里程碑。”据IT之家了解，欧几里得望远镜于 2023 年从美国佛罗里达州发射升空，目前正在收集有关宇宙膨胀过程、宇宙结构随时间演化的数据，同时研究暗能量和暗物质的本质，以及引力在宇宙大尺度结构中发挥的作用。佩托里诺表示：“欧几里得不仅会拍摄天空中星系的二维图像，还会测量它们的距离，从而获得第三个维度。这将帮助我们了解星系在太空和时间中的位置，追溯长达 100 亿年的宇宙历史，并观测银河系平面以外各个方向的宇宙。”她进一步解释说：“星系沿着丝状结构聚集，周围则分布着大片空旷区域，最终形成一个我们称之为‘宇宙网’的网络结构。欧几里得将重建这张宇宙网，并揭示它随时间推移的演化过程。”“这项研究非常重要，因为宇宙网的具体形态，包括其中存在多少星系团和空洞，以及这些结构的演化速度，都取决于暗能量和暗物质的性质。”宇宙主要由普通物质、暗物质和暗能量构成。普通物质包括恒星、行星、气体、尘埃以及地球上人类熟悉的各种物质，约占宇宙总组成的 5%。暗物质无法直接观测，但科学家可以通过它在星系尺度上产生的引力效应推断其存在，预计约占宇宙总组成的 27%。暗能量则被认为是推动宇宙加速膨胀的原因，预计约占 68%。暗物质和暗能量都不会发射或吸收光，因此无法通过常规观测手段直接看到。此前，欧几里得任务公布的数据仅涉及数天的观测结果。此次发布的数据则涵盖了超过一年的观测记录，但目前仅占望远镜未来六年观测计划中可见光和近红外波段目标天空总面积的 14%。这批数据还将在明年迎来进一步补充，届时研究团队将公布首批有关暗能量和暗物质的研究成果。引力透镜效应来自遥远星系的光在抵达地球的过程中，可能受到前景普通物质和暗物质的影响，发生弯曲和扭曲。这种现象被称为引力透镜效应。简单来说，前方星系的引力会改变来自后方星系的光线传播路径。引力透镜效应是科学家研究暗物质分布的重要工具。此次公布的欧几里得观测数据中，包含约 1.5 万个强引力透镜候选目标，数量超过此前半个世纪以来人类发现的总和。英国朴次茅斯大学天体物理学博士生、欧几里得科学家联盟成员娜塔莉 · 莱恩斯（Natalie Lines）表示：“引力透镜就像大自然自带的称重工具。”她解释说：“光线弯曲的程度能够告诉我们一个星系包含多少物质，其中也包括暗物质等不可见成分。通过研究数千个引力透镜，我们可以了解暗物质在星系中的分布情况，进而弄清星系在宇宙漫长历史中如何形成和演化。”莱恩斯还特别提到了欧几里得望远镜在大范围宇宙观测中展现出的成像清晰度。她表示：“地面望远镜能够观测夜空中的大片区域，但受到大气层影响，拍摄的图像往往不够清晰。哈勃空间望远镜和詹姆斯 · 韦布空间望远镜能够拍摄非常清晰的图像，但观测范围通常只有天空中的一小块区域。欧几里得则能够同时实现这两点。对于发现强引力透镜这类数量稀少、目标较小的天体而言，这一点至关重要。”由于遥远天体发出的光需要经过漫长时间才能抵达地球，因此观测距离越远，实际上也就意味着我们看到的是越久远的宇宙历史。目前，欧几里得望远镜观测到的最遥远天体是类星体。这类天体是由超大质量黑洞驱动的星系明亮核心，亮度极高。欧几里得已经精准定位了约 6000 万个类星体。莱恩斯表示：“欧几里得已经发现了一些非常古老的类星体，它们形成于宇宙当前年龄仅为 5% 的时期。这意味着，我们如今接收到的光线，大约在 130 亿年前就已经从这些天体出发。”

articles.title: 比亚迪腾势汽车李慧谈“速成车”：我们宁愿慢一点，也绝不在安全上“抄近路”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，今天晚间的腾势 N8 上市发布会伊始，比亚迪腾势汽车总经理李慧就谈到了“速成车”。李慧直言，今年的车市非常热闹，前 10 个月平均每天有 3 场发布会。热闹之下，行业内诞生了一个扎心的词 ——“速成车”。“速成车”压缩的是消费者看不见、摸不着，但又关乎安全底线的验证环节。这种走捷径的方式，是把用户当成免费的试车员。他透露，腾势 N8 于 2023 年 8 月正式立项，至今打磨了整整三年多，完成了冬测、夏测等大量安全类测试，一个都没有省，直到全部通过。腾势 N8 的测试数据是真实数据，绝不是 AI 生成。“在腾势造车体系中，安全是底线。我们宁愿慢一点，也绝不在安全上抄近路。…… 千锤百炼，只为让用户买车不烧心。”发布会上，李慧还引用了百年药店“同仁堂”的古训：炮制虽繁必不敢省人工，品味虽贵必不敢减物力。据IT之家了解，腾势 N8 共推出 6 款配置车型，官方指导价区间为 26.99 万-32.99 万元。新车先期仅提供纯电动版本，插电混动车型后续推出。相关阅读：《比亚迪腾势 N8 正式上市：搭载 30 英寸全景屏 + 天际屏，售 26.99 万元起》

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，黄仁勋辞去英伟达总裁、首席执行官及董事会成员职务后，成为英伟达首任董事会主席的哈维 · 琼斯（Harvey Jones）向英伟达员工发布内部备忘录。琼斯拥有超过 30 年的创业、科技企业管理和风险投资经验，曾任新思科技 CEO 及执行董事长。路透社获得了备忘录的副本，IT之家附译文如下：各位英伟达员工：我写信是想向大家通报一项重要决定。黄仁勋已辞去首席执行官及董事会成员职务，董事会已委任首席财务官（CFO）科莱特 · 克雷斯（Colette Kress）出任临时首席执行官；与此同时，董事会将面向内外部候选人遴选常任继任者。我将出任公司有史以来的首任董事会主席。在担任首席财务官的 13 年多时间里，科莱特一直是英伟达业务增长与资本战略的关键缔造者之一。她对公司业务及所处市场有着极为深刻的理解。董事会对科莱特充满信心，相信她能够带领公司履行对股东、客户、合作伙伴以及每一位员工的承诺。黄仁勋为英伟达作出了深远贡献。英伟达是全球最具影响力的科技企业之一。我们开创了加速计算，定义了现代 GPU，并打造了驱动人工智能发展的核心平台。董事会深感责任重大，定当恪尽职守，守护好这家伟大的企业。英伟达的力量源泉在于全体员工、领导团队、技术实力以及合作伙伴生态系统。我坚信，在科莱特的领导和董事会的全力支持下，公司业务将持续增长，并继续引领行业前行。感谢大家的专注投入、专业精神以及对英伟达的坚定奉献。哈维 · 琼斯英伟达董事会主席Dear NVIDIA Employees,I am writing to share an important update. Jensen has resigned as CEO and Board Member, and the Board has asked our Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress to serve as interim CEO while it conducts a search for a permanent successor looking at both internal and external candidates. I will serve as the first-ever Chair of the Board.As CFO for over 13 years, Colette has been a key architect of NVIDIA’s growth and capital strategy. She possesses a deep understanding of this business and the markets in which we operate. The Board has full confidence in Colette to deliver on our commitments to shareholders, customers, partners, and to each of you.Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. We pioneered accelerated computing, defined the modern GPU, and built the platform that powered artificial intelligence.The Board takes seriously our duty as stewards of this great company.The strength of this company resides in our employees, leadership team, technical strength and partner ecosystem. I am confident that under Colette’s leadership, with the full support of the Board, we will continue to grow our business, and lead the industry forward. Thank you for your focus, your professionalism, and your commitment to NVIDIA.Harvey JonesChair, NVIDIA Board of Director

articles.title: 谷歌为 Android XR 智能眼镜推出全面隐私保护措施：录制指示灯、人脸模糊与数据即删
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，谷歌与 Warby Parker、Gentle Monster 合作推出的首款 Android XR 智能眼镜，正面临一个不太容易解决的问题：如何摆脱消费者对智能眼镜的隐私担忧。由于早期进入这一领域的厂商没有充分重视隐私保护，智能眼镜逐渐背上了“偷拍眼镜”的负面标签。部分用户甚至将其视为侵犯他人隐私的工具。以 Meta 智能眼镜为例，这款产品曾因被不法分子滥用而饱受争议。一些人会设法关闭眼镜上用于提示正在拍摄的 LED 指示灯，或者利用眼镜做出令人反感的行为。Meta 此前对录制内容的处理方式也曾引发隐私争议。这些问题叠加在一起，让消费者对智能眼镜产生了不信任，也使其背上了负面社会标签。谷歌其实也不是毫无前车之鉴。早在第一代 Google Glass 推出时，用户就曾因佩戴这款眼镜而遭到嘲讽，甚至被冠以“Glasshole”（可理解为戴着智能眼镜四处惹人反感的人）的称呼。显然，谷歌从当年的经历中吸取了不少教训。这其实有些可惜，因为摄像头对于智能眼镜而言具有很强的实用价值。用户可以用它随手拍照，而内置 AI 助手也能借助摄像头理解用户眼前的环境。但如今由于隐私争议，这项功能反而让人觉得有些不自在。带着这样的背景，来看看谷歌准备如何处理这个敏感问题。首先，所有 Android XR 智能眼镜都配备了一个朝外的指示灯，其作用与 Meta 智能眼镜上的隐私 LED 类似。不过，两者有一个重要区别：Android XR 眼镜上的指示灯实际上是“录制指示灯”。只要眼镜正在拍摄能够以某种形式保存、供用户日后查看的内容，指示灯就会亮起。例如，用户拍照或录制视频时，指示灯都会启动。但如果用户只是调用 Gemini 获取周围环境的信息，指示灯则不会亮起。这是因为，所有用于 Gemini 的摄像头画面都会在使用后立即删除。这些图像不会出现在 Gemini 的聊天记录中，而且用户也无法选择保留。换句话说，无论用户还是谷歌，都无法在之后重新调用这些图像。谷歌还明确表示，不会将 Gemini 获取的这些图像用于 AI 模型训练或广告投放。此外，用户可以自行控制 Android XR 眼镜上的哪些应用有权使用摄像头。更重要的是，谷歌还专门考虑了如何防止有人擅自破坏指示灯的隐私保护功能。Android XR 眼镜会定期自动执行系统检查，确认指示灯是否正常工作。用户在给眼镜充电时，可能会看到指示灯交替闪烁白光和蓝光，这实际上就是系统在检查相关硬件是否运行正常。如果系统发现指示灯出现故障，眼镜就会自动禁用摄像头。另一项让人印象深刻的设计，是谷歌对周围其他人的隐私保护。当用户通过 Intelligent Eyewear 将照片发送给 Gemini 时，手机会在照片发送之前，自动对画面中的人脸进行模糊处理。这项操作直接在手机本地完成，属于智能眼镜配套应用的一部分。类似地，发送给 Gemini 的语音数据也会经过过滤，尽可能去除用户本人以外的其他人的声音。语音过滤只是谷歌利用麦克风实现隐私保护的一个例子。另一个例子是实时翻译功能：该功能主要针对用户前方 60 度范围内的声音进行识别，同时过滤周围环境中的其他声音。在摄像头与 Gemini 的交互方式上，谷歌还向 9to5Google 解释称，Gemini 经过专门调整，不会在用户没有明确表达意图时随意调用摄像头。例如，用户询问“这幅画是什么”，显然意味着希望眼镜观察眼前的场景，并识别这件艺术品。在这种情况下，Gemini 可以直接调用摄像头。但如果用户问的是“桌子上有多少钱”，谷歌认为，仅凭这句话还不能确定用户是否希望启用摄像头。因此，Gemini 会先向用户追问确认，而不是直接拍摄眼前的画面。除了摄像头调用机制，谷歌还通过限制录制时长来降低智能眼镜被滥用的风险。谷歌将 Intelligent Eyewear 的单次视频录制时长限制在 90 秒以内。这确实会限制用户的部分使用场景，但谷歌表示，大多数实际录制任务本来就不会超过这一时长。作为对比，Meta 智能眼镜支持最长 5 分钟的视频录制。除了智能眼镜配套应用和 Gemini 本身，谷歌还表示，将通过旗下其他产品和服务采取措施，防止 Android XR 眼镜的摄像头遭到滥用，具体包括：负责任使用要求：用户首次使用智能眼镜前，必须同意相关使用规则，包括未经他人许可不得拍摄他人、不得在敏感场所进行拍摄，以及不得遮挡录制指示灯。违反这些规定将构成对谷歌服务条款的违约，用户使用智能眼镜的权限可能因此被禁用。Google Shopping 和 Google Ads：谷歌禁止在购物平台销售、在广告中推广专门用于遮挡录制指示灯的贴纸或配件。Google Play：谷歌禁止应用利用摄像头进行社交直播或实时人脸识别，也不允许应用擅自改变眼镜外部指示灯

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，今天晚间，英伟达临时 CEO 科莱特 · 克雷斯向全体员工发出内部备忘录。路透社获得了备忘录的副本，其内容如下：各位英伟达同事：我对公司和公司的未来充满信心。更重要的是，我相信在座的每一位员工，相信我们的客户和合作伙伴，也相信我们每天都在全球经济中发挥着不可或缺的作用。董事会、高管团队和我都深知，过去这段时间对大家来说极其艰难。感谢各位在困难时期展现出的坚韧、专业素养，以及始终如一的敬业精神。公司能够取得今天的成就，靠的是每一位员工日复一日的付出。你们是公司最宝贵的力量。未来几天，管理层会进一步向大家介绍公司的未来发展。我们还将在 11 月 18 日美国太平洋时间上午 9 时召开全员会议。我们肩负着开发 AI 革命核心技术的重要使命，接下来还有许多重要工作要做。让我们继续并肩前行，保持一直以来的坚定信念和敬业精神。感谢大家的所有付出。科莱特 "Dear NVIDIANs,I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy.The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication. Thank you.This company has achieved so much because of the work that all of you bring to it every single day. You are our greatest strength. You will hear more from leadership in the coming days about our future together, and we will host a company meeting on November 18 at 9 a.m. PT.We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us. So let's move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company.Thank you for all you do,Colette"黄仁勋辞去总裁、首席执行官及董事会成员职务后，英伟达任命执行副总裁兼首席财务官科莱特 · 克雷斯（Colette Kress）为临时首席执行官。在正式继任者确定之前，克雷斯在代行首席执行官职责的同时，将继续兼任执行副总裁兼首席财务官。董事会目前已启动正式首席执行官的遴选工作，并将统筹考虑内部及外部候选人。IT之家注：克雷斯拥有亚利桑那大学金融系的理学学士学位和南卫理公会大学工商管理硕士（MBA）学位。自 2013 年 9 月加入英伟达以来，克雷斯一直担任执行副总裁兼首席财务官。英伟达表示，任职期间，她全面领导公司财务部门，在英伟达的业务增长与发展演进中发挥了关键作用。克雷斯曾在思科业务技术和运营财务部门担任了三年的高级副总裁兼首席财务官，负责所有业务部门、工程部门和运营部门的财务战略制定、计划、报告和业务发展。此前，克雷斯在微软公司工作了 13 年，包括在服务器和工具部门担任首席财务官的 4 年，还担任过企业规划与财务领域的高级职务。在此之前，克雷斯还曾在德州仪器担任过多个财务职位。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，英伟达今日发布 GeForce Game Ready 621.24 显卡驱动，新版本为《战锤 40000：战争黎明 4》（Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV）以及《神力科莎：拉力赛》（Assetto Corsa Rally）提供最佳游戏体验，并配合《燕云十六声》（Where Winds Meet）新增搭载 3D 引导神经渲染（3D-Guided Neural Rendering）的 DLSS 5 技术。据 IT 之家查证，《战锤 40000：战争黎明 4》由 KING Art 开发，原定 9 月 17 日发售，后延期至 12 月 3 日正式上线，指挥官版玩家可于 11 月 30 日抢先进入游戏，本次驱动正为此提前进行适配优化。此前英伟达官方预告，DLSS 5 本月将登陆《战争雷霆》与《燕云十六声》，本次随驱动落地后者。新游戏支持与性能优化《战锤 40000：战争黎明 4》：提供发售前性能优化与最佳游戏体验支持《神力科莎：拉力赛》（Assetto Corsa Rally）：提供 Game Ready 优化支持《燕云十六声》：游戏新增搭载 3D 引导神经渲染的 DLSS 5 技术，RTX 显卡玩家可借此提升帧率与画面表现问题修复修复 Chaos Vantage 中 NVIDIA OptiX 降噪器 在高分辨率下可能失效的问题（问题编号 6953474）修复 Windows 照片应用 / 媒体播放器播放大疆 D-Log H.265 视频时色彩显示异常的问题（问题编号 6996250）官方本次更新日志未列出针对游戏崩溃、花屏、卡顿类问题的专项修复。IT之家附官方公告链接（https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/warhammer-40000-dawn-of-war-4-geforce-rtx-spark-game-ready-driver/）。该驱动适配 GeForce RTX、GTX 系列桌面端及笔记本显卡，支持 Windows 10 与 Windows 11 系统，有对应游戏需求的玩家可通过 GeForce Experience 或英伟达官网下载更新。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，本田今天（12 日）晚间宣布，第七代 CR-V 将于 2027 年上市，作为 2028 款车型，全系搭载全新 Honda Hybrid 双电机混动系统。新车还将换用全新平台，大幅提升动力性能和燃油经济性，同时延续 CR-V 过去 30 年来的“高性价比和实用性”。据悉，2028 款 CR-V 将首次搭载第五代双电机混动系统，在性能和燃油经济性方面进一步升级。通过扩大发动机的高效运行区间、提高混动驱动单元的效率等改进，本田进一步优化了混动系统。此外，新车还将配备全新开发的电动四驱系统，能够更精准、更迅速地控制电机。第七代 CR-V 也将率先采用本田全新开发的平台，通过多项创新技术兼顾车身刚性和轻量化，并利用模块化设计提高零部件通用率。本田希望借此进一步提升驾驶乐趣，为车主带来更具运动感和激情的驾驶体验。IT之家从新闻稿获悉，本田计划将下一代混动车型的燃油经济性提升 10% 以上，同时进一步改善驾驶体验。去年 10 月，本田在日本展示了全新大型车混动系统的核心技术，计划用于未来仅在美国生产的大型车型。新系统采用全新开发的 V6 发动机、驱动单元和电池组，兼顾强劲动力、较高的拖拽能力和出色的环保性能。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，三星终于开始为旗下首款智能眼镜接受预订，这款产品名为 Intelligent Eyewear，今天起在韩国和美国开启预售，将于 12 月 10 日开始发货。三星将与合作眼镜品牌 Gentle Monster 和 Warby Parker 联合推出 Intelligent Eyewear，共提供 30 种不同设计，售价为 395 至 489 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,641 至 3,269 元人民币）。其中，Gentle Monster 提供 6 种镜框款式，共有 16 种配置；Warby Parker 则提供 3 种镜框设计，共有 14 种配置。Gentle Monster 系列包括以下款式：镜框造型：方形、圆形、超大尺寸棱角形、猫眼形、窄矩形和椭圆形。镜框颜色：黑色、酒红色、白色 / 浅灰色。Warby Parker 系列包括以下款式：镜框造型：经典方形 / 矩形、圆形。镜框颜色：黑色、深绿色、深红色 / 棕色。消费者可以通过 Warby Parker 的线上商店和实体门店、Gentle Monster 官方线上商店，以及部分三星零售门店预订这款眼镜。如果想在购买前亲自体验，可以从 2026 年 12 月 10 日起，前往指定门店试用。三星 Intelligent Eyewear 配备一颗 1200 万像素前置摄像头、四个麦克风和两颗开放式扬声器。借助摄像头和麦克风，眼镜能够感知用户看到的画面、听到的声音，进而利用 AI 帮助用户完成各种任务。系统方面，这款眼镜运行谷歌 Android XR 操作系统，同时搭载 Gemini 和 Bixby 两款 AI 助手。不过，Bixby 仅在眼镜与三星 Galaxy 手机配对时才能使用。硬件方面，眼镜搭载高通骁龙 AR1 Gen 1 处理器，配备 2GB 内存和 64GB 存储空间。三星表示，眼镜与配对智能手机会分担运算任务。用户可以通过语音指令和触控手势操作这款设备。兼容性方面，三星 Galaxy S 系列和 Galaxy Z 系列手机需要运行 One UI 9.0 或更新版本。此外，这款眼镜也支持苹果 iPhone（iPhone 13 及更新机型，内存至少为 6GB）和谷歌 Pixel 手机（Pixel 7 及更新机型）。影像方面，1200 万像素摄像头支持拍照，还能录制最高 3K 分辨率、30fps 的 SDR 视频，或者录制 2K HDR 视频。连接方面，眼镜支持 Wi-Fi 6E 和蓝牙 5.4。续航方面，眼镜单次充电后，在混合使用场景下最长可使用 9 小时。配合随附的充电盒，总续航时间最长可达 72 小时。按照每天使用约 10 小时计算，充电盒能够提供约一周的使用时间。这款眼镜平均重量为 41 克，具备 IPX4 级防水能力，可抵御各个方向的溅水。其中，Gentle Monster 款式重量为 39.6 至 43.9 克，Warby Parker 款式则为 40.4 至 42.6 克。三星表示，第一代智能眼镜主要面向导航、语言翻译和视觉辅助等使用场景。得益于与谷歌 Gemini AI 助手的深度整合，Intelligent Eyewear 能够识别地标和各类物体，并根据识别结果回答用户进一步提出的问题。眼镜还可以通过互联网或用户的谷歌账户获取信息，回答日常问题。在实际使用中，这款眼镜支持实时语言翻译，还能通过谷歌地图提供逐步导航指引。用户也可以利用眼镜拍摄白板内容或会议笔记，并将相关内容直接整理、总结到三星 Notes 应用中。此外，借助 AI 功能，眼镜还能朗读手机收到的通知，并根据上下文自动对通知进行分类和摘要整理，以更自然的语言向用户传达信息。

articles.title: 姚期智杨植麟首次联手给 AI 出的博士级题目，Kimi 多画出了「关键一条边」
articles.content: Kimi 刷新 629 条边图论参考纪录，只多加了1条边，为什么数学界等了这么多年？    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       给 124 个点连线，不能出现三角形，也不能出现四边形。此前的参考记录是 629 条——数学界认为这已经接近极限。而Kimi K3 构造出了 630 条边的图，并通过程序验证。多1条边，听起来不多。但在组合数学里，你每试图多塞进一条边，都需要在全图 124 个点之间重新完成一次精密的结构大重构。这1条边意味着AI第一次在“极值构造”这类研究级任务上，把人类参考纪录往前推了一步。这项成果来自图灵奖得主、中科院院士、清华大学交叉信息研究院院长姚期智与月之暗面创始人杨植麟等人的联合研究。他们真正想回答的问题是：AI到底能不能做数学研究，而不只是做数学题？01「多 1 条边」算不算真突破？姚期智，图灵奖得主、清华大学交叉信息研究院院长，是中国理论计算机科学的奠基者之一；杨植麟，月之暗面创始人，Kimi背后的推动者。两代人、两种身份：一位是理论计算机科学的泰斗，一位是大模型创业的一线操盘手，第一次联合署名。这个组合本身就说明了一件事：AI做科研，已经不是“实验室里的猜想”，而是需要理论计算机科学家和大模型团队坐在一起定义“什么叫算做出来了”。但在另一面，争议同样如影随形：多构造出一条边，到底算不算真正的科学突破？这算不算只是暴力搜索蒙对的个例？AI真懂背后的数学机理吗？这正是姚期智团队的核心初衷。如果无法区分‘运气好撞上’和‘逻辑上证明’，AI 就永远只是个黑盒计算器。于是，他们没有继续在传统基准上打转，而是联手搭了一套前所未有的评测系统——TCSExam。为回答这个问题，他们提出 TCSExam，用 100 项理论计算机科学科研任务，测试前沿 AI Agent 能否证明定理、开发 Solver、构造数学对象，甚至挑战长期未解决的猜想。论文地址：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.07962v1实验中，GPT-6 Astra 完成了 20 项研究级定理中的 14 项，还将一个有限域矩阵猜想在特定条件下的已知证明范围从 8 维推进到了 9 维。TCSExam 的核心创新，是将 AI 科研能力转化为可以独立验证的研究成果。 它通过 Lean 4、程序检查器和 Checkpoint 机制，分别验证数学证明、算法表现及中间推导，避免把局部进展误判为完整成果。其中，Astra 的 9 维证明将复杂的矩阵问题压缩为整数约束，最终利用 143 条方程构造出可核验的矛盾证书。从任务形式化、研究证书设计到数学证明的自动检查，这套框架展示了 AI 参与真实科研的一条技术路径。02TCSExam 如何建立评测框架？一句话：把“AI 做科研”拆成四条可验证的轨道，再用三层机制防止“局部进展被误判为完整成果”。普通数学考试有标准答案，而理论计算机科学涉及的研究工作差异很大，有的需要证明新定理，有的需要开发最优算法，有的要构造满足约束的数学对象。这些成果的形式不同，评价方式也必须随之调整。研究团队因此将 100 项任务划分为四条轨道：定理证明（20 项）：覆盖 13 个理论计算机科学领域，要求模型提交 Lean 4 证明。Solver 工程（30 项）：要求开发可重复运行的算法程序，在独立测试实例和统一资源限制下评测；数学构造（20 项）：考察模型能否生成符合严格约束的图、纠错码等对象；开放猜想（30 项）：允许模型从证明成立或寻找反例两个方向展开研究。雷峰网任务划分之后，更复杂的问题出现在数学语言的转换过程中。人类研究者能够理解一段定理描述，但机器验证需要明确的定义、量词、假设和参数范围。任何一个条件发生变化，最终证明的数学含义就可能不同。例如，一个定理原本要求某种性质对任意规模的图成立，如果转写成 Lean 时额外增加了图规模限制，那么模型即使完成证明，也

articles.content: 这三个问题不解决，数据终究会成为具身最大卡点，一位前微软亚研科学家的“提前量”。    作者丨邓哲敏    编辑丨齐铖湧                                                                                                       今年初秋，Skild S1、Generalist GEN-1.5、RoboTTT 等工作密集亮相，不约而同将上下文学习（ICL）带入机器学习领域。AI科技评论（雷峰网）注意到，国内一支团队也在同一时间发布了能够实现上下文学习的世界模型，领头羊是清华大学智能产业研究院（AIR）教授曹婷。2009 年，曹婷赴澳洲读博，师从编程语言与系统领域的两位顶尖学者，研究非对称多核处理器与 Java 这类托管语言之间功耗与性能的权衡。博士期间所著论文入选 CACM 研究亮点，图灵奖得主大卫·帕特森专门撰文推荐，并收录进自己的经典教材《计算机体系结构：量化研究方法》。值得一提的是一篇发表在 ISCA 的论文：The Yin and Yang of Power and Performance for Asymmetric Hardware and Managed Software，其论证近乎诗意：虚拟机的垃圾回收、即时编译这些额外开销，恰好是可以卸到小核上去跑的差异负载，用小核的“阳”，去补虚拟机开销的“阴”；反过来，非对称硬件暴露出来的复杂性，又正好被托管语言的抽象所化解。在我们看来，这段经历埋下了影响曹婷学术生涯的东西：一个关于阴阳的直觉——约束，从不只是限制，它也可以是逼出系统生机的起点。博士毕业后，曹婷来到华为编译器与编程语言实验室，负责方舟编译器的内存管理，在有限的内存里，让程序跑得更快更省。2018 年，她加入微软亚洲研究院（MSRA）异构计算组，一待就是七年，做端侧 AI 推理，把几十亿参数的神经网络，塞进手机、PC 和 IoT 设备，让它们不靠云端，在本地的算力、功耗和存储里跑起来。低比特量化、LUT 查表推理、存算一体加速器，这些技术进入微软 Office、Windows、Bing，服务百万级用户。2025 年夏天，曹婷加入清华 AIR。这一次，横在她面前的是更凶险的约束：训练数据极度匮乏、物理环境千变万化的现实。她很快发现，机器人在固定设置下能做对动作，环境稍有变化就失败，而那些失败里藏着的宝贵信息，又被传统系统随手丢掉。具身智能已经能做 Demo，却迟迟无法真正部署。曹婷的答案，还是“阴阳”，既然约束无法穷举，那就把约束变成养分。当年 10 月，她和 MSRA 时期的老搭档、清华 AIR 副院长刘云新教授共同发起域变换（Z-Trans），押注具身自进化，并陆续发布 Z0、Zeva、Zeva Ego、Zetta、Z-infra 等工作。从让软件在异构硬件上省功耗，到让模型在边缘设备上省算力，再到让智能在物理世界里学会自进化，曹婷这十几年做的始终是同一件事：让智能在条件不充分的情况下好好工作。以下是AI科技评论与曹婷的对话，在不改变原意的基础上有所编辑。01 当机器人工厂慢慢冷下来“整体的技术范式没有收敛，而且变化特别快，基本每个月都不一样，但一个离线、一个在线这套学习范式，应该是大家统一认可的。”▎AI科技评论：今年上半年，整个行业还在疯狂建机器人数采工厂，试图用海量数据大力出奇迹。但到了下半年，陆续出现了许多具身上下文学习的工作，是前序研究证明了什么吗？曹婷：我自己的体会非常深刻。今年 5 月份之前，大家还相信“离线训一个模型，它在线就能干活”，但现在看，这些数采工厂基本都冷掉了。大家发现，离线数据采得再多，机器人在线依然干不成活，因为离线数据永远涵盖不到真实世界的全部情况。看到之前的路走不通，大家才开始思考怎样让机器人不只依赖离线训练，还能在部署后利用新的示范和反馈进行在线的上下文学习。▎AI科技评论：大家在技术上达成共识了吗？曹婷：整体上学习范式分两种：一种 offline，一种 online。在上下文中学习这个概念最早是从大语言模型（LLM

articles.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
articles.content: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Experiments covered colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with testing on held-out data from the training source and on independent datasets from other institutions. The adapted foundation model generalised better on every external dataset. Within the training distribution, the task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant, and delineated boundaries more precisely, while the foundation model more often missed small lesions. Only a small fraction of the foundation model required adaptation, and the capacity needed was determined by the imaging domain rather than by the adaptation method. A widely used polyp test set was also found to duplicate images from another benchmark. Foundation-model adaptation is therefore warranted where models must work across sites, with capacity selected on the target domain.

articles.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
articles.content: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning. In addition, building on our previously pro posed example-based EM-DETR framework, we adapt it to jointly learn from multiple domain-specific datasets, enabling fine-grained, example driven detection across modalities. Our model achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results, with image-level AUC scores exceeding previous SOTA by 1% point on four key findings in CXRs. We achieve a leading mAP50 in CXRs and mammography, surpassing EM-DETR trained on a single dataset by 2-3% points. This approach paves the way for scalable foundation models in medical imaging that leverage heterogeneous data while maintaining robust and generalizable performance.

articles.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
articles.content: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes. The results illustrate where this generality remains computationally practical and where overhead is substantial. Library is available on GitHub at https://github.com/alexshtf/torchcurves.

articles.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
articles.content: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that the teacher identifies a different failure in each task class and shifts its scaffolds from step-by-step workflows to targeted fixes as the student improves, and that its revised scaffolds help the student learn more than keeping the previous scaffold or using no scaffold.

articles.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
articles.content: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the unit an agent proposes and scores, an existing agent can use them to re-evaluate evidence it has already collected or to guide its search. Across six domains, $89\%$ of the pointwise candidates with the largest belief shifts are rejections. On the same evidence, contrast sets resolve $73\%$ of these candidates to a specific alternative. When contrast sets guide search, the agent resolves $67\%$ more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget. In a blinded study, $38$ human experts chose the same explanation on $78\%$ of resolved questions and on $82\%$ of questions where the pointwise agent rejected its hypothesis and stopped. Together, these results support explicit competing explanations as a way for discovery agents to resolve more scientific questions from the same evidence and validation budget.

articles.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
articles.content: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls. These agents achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, exceeding observed expert performance. LLM-guided feature discovery generally outperforms direct reasoning, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves open-weight models, enabling them to match or surpass closed-source frontier models in our evaluations. These results establish Pyrite as a challenging test of pose-ranking ability and highlight LLM-guided feature discovery as a promising approach to interpret and combine the outputs of computational chemistry tools.

articles.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
articles.content: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3). The biases involved are known in machine learning (under-tuned baselines, inherited weights, winner's curse); we measure what they do to biological conclusions, using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models. Some claims survive every protocol we test: segregated reward and punishment dopamine improves learning, and head-direction topography is required for a persistent bump. Others do not. In the mushroom body, the real Kenyon-cell output wiring beats a cross-subtype identity shuffle by 0.09 under P1 and P2 but loses to it by 0.09 under P3 (95% CIs exclude zero; held-out runs confirm). The verdict is set by the share of alpha'beta' cells among active Kenyon cells, which P1 selects low; at the share implied by imaging (about 44%) the real-wiring model fails to learn, exposing a model inadequacy rather than a deficit of the fly's wiring. In flyvis, P1 penalises a mirrored connectome, which has a constructed solution within 0.07 (median) of the real error, more than a spatially shuffled one in 50 of 50 members; the ranking survives ten-fold longer retraining but depends on the checkpoint at fifty-fold. A credible structural claim needs matched optimisation, data-constrained physiology and a model that still works there.

articles.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
articles.content: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for. Each instance is scored based on the share of this feedback budget consumed. Since a learner may keep anything between instances, memory-based and weight-based systems are scored on the same scale. After the stream, the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of the tasks it met, which measures memorization, and on unseen tasks, which measures generalization. We run an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash, comparing them with two prompting floors, a program-induction method and Qwen3.5-9B's weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations, across all models we tested. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. articles.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
articles.content: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

articles.title: Measuring Robustness and Efficiency in a Connectome-Constrained Fly Visual System Model: Linking an Adversarial and a Perceptual Illusion
articles.content: Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations. Whether networks with brain-like wiring are more robust at lower computational cost is unclear. We address this by benchmarking a task-optimized, continuous-time recurrent neural network of the fly visual system constrained by its synaptic connectome (FlyNet) against artificial neural networks. We compare it against CNNs, RAFT, and continuous-time recurrent neural networks without detailed connectome constraints (sCTRNN, CTRNN) on a collision-detection task within a differentiable 3D rendering pipeline. FlyNet is adversarially vulnerable but, relative to its compute, more robust to common video corruptions than RAFT, while using up to five orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs. The CTRNNs remain more robust than FlyNet across almost all tested perturbations, suggesting that connectome constraints benefit efficiency, through their low edge count, over robustness. Recurrence improves robustness to white-box attacks in RAFT and temporal context improves robustness to common corruptions. FlyNet's position and velocity representations degrade under adversarial textures but recover under counterfactual textures that restore correct classification while staying equally far from training, ruling out unfamiliar textures as the cause of failure. The reverse-phi illusion similarly disrupts these representations and inverts the same low-level motion statistic as the adversarial textures. Optimizing this input statistic alone, without access to the network, suffices to induce classification failure, attributing both perturbations to the same circuit vulnerability. Connectome-constrained models can thus surface adversarial failure mechanisms as testable hypotheses about biological perceptual vulnerabilities.

articles.title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval
articles.content: Cross-sensor remote sensing image retrieval aims to find scenes with the same content across heterogeneous sensors, such as SAR and optical or panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) imagery, without manual labels. Existing self-supervised methods either reconstruct sensor-specific pixel detail, align each image only with its co-registered twin, or rely on large transformers with 118-173M parameters (and up to 398M). We introduce RS-JEPA, a compact joint-embedding predictive framework built on a Vision Mamba encoder shared by both sensors. Since a state-space encoder reads an image as an ordered sequence of patches, we propose scan-path views, which treat two reading orders of the same image as two views with identical pixels and predict the hidden patches in one order from the visible patches in the other.To keep this prediction challenging, we propose Adversarial View Coupling (AVC), which learns the hardest split of the visible patches, and a neighbourhood consensus loss that aligns the scene similarities of both sensors. Extensive experiments on SAR-optical (BEN-14K, CBRSIR-VS) and PAN-MS (DSRSID) benchmarks demonstrate that RS-JEPA achieves the highest F1@5 among twelve re-implemented methods (72.92, 80.35 and 94.43) with a retrieval network of only 3.88M parameters (14.57M in training, 8-16times fewer than prior JEPA retrievers). Like prior methods, RS-JEPA trains on co-registered pairs. Our results highlight reading order as a source of self-supervised views. code: https://github.com/Tanishq251/RSJEPA.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
articles.content: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. Our results demonstrate that (1) the information available to the evaluation harness determines evaluation quality, (2) functional and security evaluation are complementary, and (3) LLM-based evaluation harnesses surface subtle errors that human reviewers miss. We recommend a two-framework strategy: trace-based evaluation for functional assessment and adversarial red-teaming for security validation.

articles.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
articles.content: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. The agent's reasoning, the explanation it writes with each tool call, often states why it took an action; the tool calls alone do not. ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it. Only this last stage depends on the platform, so rule documents can be compiled for different orchestration platforms. On $79$ procedures from our production platform, ReTrace workflows reach $93.8\%$ completion, against $96.8\%$ for the agent, at $24\%$ lower cost per task. On $τ^2$-Bench, they reach $75.8\%$ task success (agent: $80.6\%$) and run in $1.3$s instead of $170$s; three rounds of repair on training failures lift $k{=}2$ workflows from $66.7\%$ to $81.2\%$. On eight SOP-Bench procedures, ReTrace without repair trails few-shot generation ($80.6\%$ vs. $83.6\%$), but repair from labeled training failures lifts it to $87.8\%$ at $0.40$s per task, compared to $85.5\%$ in $46.6$s for the agent.

articles.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
articles.content: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.

articles.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
articles.content: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress. It cuts success from 47 to 16 of 50 on one task and from 44 to 10 on the other. When the same frames are withheld from memory, success returns, so the cause lies in memory rather than in the interruption itself. We trace the failure to a temporal shortcut: because demonstrations proceed at a steady pace, elapsed time predicts progress. Indeed, rescaling the time stamps alone makes the policy stop early when the clock runs fast and repeat when it runs slow. Surprisingly, removing the time encoding does not cure the failure, because the frames of a null event still occupy slots of the time-sampled memory. Across RoboMME's released designs, vulnerability follows how memory is indexed. Of the fixes the diagnosis suggests, training with injected pauses does not remove the failure and impairs counting, whereas indexing memory by events recovers half or more of the loss without retraining. A memory meant to remember what happened should count events rather than clock ticks.

articles.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
articles.content: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress. We introduce Re-Search, which adapts the format of Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only the research problem of a published paper, a model must rediscover the paper's core idea by asking yes-or-no questions. Built from 200 ICML 2026 papers, Re-Search tracks how a model's idea evolves as it asks questions and receives binary oracle feedback, isolating ideation from execution. Across six recent LLMs, nearly all progress happens within the first 30 of 100 questions, which largely decide how the game ends; after that, most models plateau. Through controlled interventions on the candidate questions and the hypothesis space, we find that the bottleneck is generation, not judgment: models recognize a good idea or a good question when one is offered, but often cannot produce it on their own. We further analyze the ideation traces and find that models fail by either over-exploiting one direction or over-exploring too many. These findings point to concrete design principles for autoresearch systems: since models can judge candidates they cannot produce, enriching the search with externally sourced ideas and questions may be more effective than improving any single model's generation ability.

articles.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference
articles.content: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry. Recent progress in mechanistic interpretability (MI) has made it possible to identify neurons, features, circuits, population structures, and dynamical patterns associated with model behavior. As these tools improve, attention is shifting from what can be observed inside a model to how those observations support mechanistic explanations. We examine the parallel efforts of neuroscience and MI to address this question and identify recurring inferential bottlenecks when inferring mechanisms from complex neural systems. We propose five principles and organize them into a recursive logic for a more rigorous procedure of mechanistic inference. These principles provide a framework that supports scientific discovery in two senses: it helps turn local interpretability findings into cumulative knowledge of mechanisms within models, and it makes those mechanisms sufficiently precise to generate testable hypotheses about domains beyond the models. Evidence beyond MI is ultimately required to establish what model mechanisms reveal about the world.

articles.title: FERN: Cross-Benchmark Table Retrieval for Text-to-SQL with Frozen Retrievers and Learned Ranking
articles.content: Text-to-SQL systems over large pooled catalogs must first retrieve the tables a question needs. We compare against the published table recall of RASL, which uses Claude 3.5 models to extract keywords and select tables, on pooled BIRD, Spider, and Fiben catalogs. FERN (Feature-Engineered Ranking with No generative LLM) instead fuses three frozen retrievers into 100 candidates, describes each with up to 120 features, and reorders them with LightGBM rankers fitted once on BIRD's training questions. On Spider, where it was not fitted, its candidate pool alone reaches RASL's published recall at fifteen tables (98.0), and the ranker raises the share of questions with every gold table in the top five (complete@5) from 83.9% to 95.6%. At five tables, FERN's recall is within one point of RASL's on Spider (96.7 vs 97.0) and on BIRD with its evidence hints (96.6 vs 97.5), and 8.2 points below on BIRD without them (89.3). On 121 real BEAVER questions, without BEAVER fitting, its recall at fifteen (82.1) falls between two BEAVER-trained retrievers (80.8, 84.5), but its complete@15 is below both (49.6 vs 54.5 and 62.0). On Fiben, it falls far short at fifteen tables (54.2 vs 69.2, different question sets), although its recall at fifty is numerically close to RASL's question-only retrieval result (80.7 vs 79.4). On BIRD dev with evidence, non-retrieval features raise complete@5 by 7.7 points over retrieval signals alone. On BIRD dev, median latency is 208 ms per question on one A100, without hosted model calls.

articles.title: BoviShift: A Six-Year Multi-Attribute Audit of Visual Cattle Phenotyping Across Animals and Time
articles.content: Computer vision offers a scalable, non-contact means of estimating livestock traits, but correlated images and video frames make reliable evaluation difficult. Image-random splitting can place views of the same animal in both training and test sets, while deployment further requires transfer to animals captured in future years. We introduce BoviShift, a corpus reconstructed from six consecutive annual cohorts of an operational cattle marketplace collected from 2021 to 2026. It contains 2{,}657 cattle, 10{,}610 still images, and 2{,}566 walk-around videos across nine recorded breed categories. We evaluate three splitting strategies through four configurations: image-random and pooled cattle-disjoint splits over the same development cohorts, followed by separate future-2025 and locked future-2026 evaluations. Using a fixed ResNet-50 multi-task baseline, we assess weight, age, height, breed, and coat color. Differences between image-random and cattle-disjoint splitting are task-dependent rather than a universal leakage penalty. Future-cohort behavior is also attribute- and cohort-specific: breed declines relative to pooled evaluation; mean weight and age performance fails to beat constant baselines in 2025; height remains above baseline; and color transfers well to 2025 but degrades in 2026. Multi-task training improves all five point estimates in a single-seed ablation, still-view aggregation helps selectively, and zero-shot video-frame aggregation exposes a still-to-video domain gap. To our knowledge, BoviShift is the longest-spanning cattle-vision resource combining consecutive annual cohorts with physical and visual attributes.

articles.title: TanCRAFT: Context-Reasoned Anticipatory Feedback for Assembly Tasks
articles.content: Preventing human error in physical assembly tasks requires assistance systems that can intervene before mistakes are made. This is especially challenging in settings where users are free to choose the construction order and correctness depends on the evolving assembly rather than a fixed next step. We present TanCRAFT, a four-stage real-time predictive assistance system that tracks the scene state, reasons about the current partial assembly, forecasts the near-future motion of manipulated pieces, and intervenes when the predicted placement is incompatible with the target. We instantiate our framework and confirm its effectiveness in a controlled tangram assembly task through offline benchmarks and a within-subject user study. Our findings show that the predictive feedback significantly reduces mistakes relative to unguided and reactive sessions, while yielding the lowest mean perceived workload and shortest mean completion time. Overall, these results demonstrate the value of predictive feedback for error prevention and provide a step toward cost-aware assistance for automation and human-robot workcells.

articles.title: C$^2$-Routing: Complementary Cropping and Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Inference
articles.content: Visual Question Answering (VQA) imposes substantial computational overhead on vision-language models (VLMs), motivating model-agnostic input reduction methods that can be readily applied across diverse VLMs, including in black-box settings. Simply enforcing a visual-token cap reduces computation, but it can discard information needed to answer the question. A single reduction strategy also struggles to accommodate different scenarios. Our key observation is that cropping and compression are complementary: cropping highlights small targets and local details, whereas whole-image compression better preserves context for large targets or distributed evidence. Based on this observation, we propose C$^2$-Routing, which adaptively selects cropping or compression according to the input image and question. Since both strategies may still discard key information, we further design a safety gate that uses the predicted joint correctness distribution under original and reduced inputs to guide fallback and protect accuracy. To accommodate consumer GPU resource constraints, all training and evaluation experiments run on RTX 3090 GPUs. To measure gains beyond token capping, we use full-image baselines with the same cap of 1,024 visual tokens. We conduct extensive evaluation on three VLMs and 18 datasets spanning local details, global scenes, scene text, and documents. With the visual budget already capped, C$^2$-Routing further reduces end-to-end FLOPs by 36.53% and visual tokens by 42.36% on average, with a mean relative task-score decrease of only 0.77%.

articles.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
articles.content: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.

articles.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
articles.content: Policy optimization is central to language model post-training, yet principled guidance remains limited. We revisit its theoretical foundations to identify algorithms that learn near-optimal policies using total samples and gradient steps governed by the base model's response coverage, a measure of how readily it generates optimal responses. We call such algorithms coverage-preserving. This guarantee captures the goal of amplifying capabilities accessible through sampling from the base model.   (1) Coverage collapse. REINFORCE, the basis for PPO and GRPO, can drive the probability of optimal responses to near zero, even as reward improves. This coverage collapse stalls optimization, and convergence can require exponentially many steps despite good initial coverage. The failure arises even with exact gradients and persists under KL regularization to the base model.   (2) Reference resets. We show that repeatedly resetting the KL reference to the most recent policy mitigates coverage collapse. We formalize this intervention in Approximate Policy Mirror Descent (APMD), a meta-algorithm that approximately solves a sequence of KL-regularized RL subproblems. APMD enables stronger regularization, making each subproblem easier to solve, while reference resets allow convergence to global optimality.   (3) Coverage-preserving algorithms. For softmax linear policies over pretrained features, we use APMD to establish the first global convergence guarantees showing that widely used families of post-training algorithms are coverage-preserving. These include stylized PPO and GRPO variants with explicit KL regularization and reference resets, and squared-loss algorithms that implement them implicitly, including those used to train the Kimi models.   These results clarify how regularization, clipping, and objective choice affect the sampling and optimization costs of post-training.

articles.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
articles.content: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second. Every observation influences the estimate in two roles, through its own evaluation when it is held out and through the models it helps fit when it trains. The random splits determine its weight in each role. From this representation, we prove an exact finite-sample identity for the variance of the cross-validated estimate. For a given splitting scheme with a common training set size, the variance is a function of these weights, with constants of the model, the metric, and the population. It covers metrics averaged over observations, such as mean squared error, and over case--control pairs, such as the AUC. The identity shows which schemes to use. The variance decomposes into sampling variance, which depends only on the training size, and variance due to the random fold splitting, which arises when the weights change from one draw of the splits to the next. K-fold cross-validation, whose weights are equal across observations by design, is therefore variance optimal at first order; Monte Carlo and bootstrap cross-validation are not. The first-order variance of K-fold does not depend on K, and under reasonable conditions on the model leave-one-out has the smallest variance of any K-fold scheme. For the AUC the same holds for leave-pair-out, which evaluates every case--control pair. Finally, we show the cross-validated estimate is asymptotically normal with the identity's full variance. Together, these results provide a general theoretical foundation for inference on cross-validated performance and establish principles for selecting variance-optimal cross-validation designs.

articles.title: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models
articles.content: We use TabPFN, a recently developed tabular foundation model, to predict three properties of energetic materials: impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature and crystal density. Without any hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN outperforms the best published models for all three properties. It also substantially outperforms a wide range of established machine-learning models, including tuned gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forests and Gaussian processes. This holds both when the models are given hand-crafted molecular descriptors and when they are given learned representations from Chemprop's message-passing neural network. TabPFN is also among the fastest models we consider, more than an order of magnitude faster than XGBoost. As TabPFN predicts the entire distribution of the target rather than just a single value, it offers built-in uncertainty quantification, which we compare with the empirical distributions of compounds with repeated measurements. Finally, we interpret the predictions using Shapley values, which rank the features by their importance.

articles.title: When does text encoding matter for language modeling?
articles.content: UTF-8's role as the de facto encoding standard in language models introduces cross-lingual inequities due to its variable-length design. However, the effect that this encoding choice has on model performance remains largely unexamined. In this work, we investigate how text encoding impacts the performance of byte-level language models, comparing UTF-8 with a wide range of other encoding strategies, including other Unicode-based approaches, language-specific encodings, and our own customized encodings. To facilitate our analysis, we propose Aether: a hybrid encoding scheme that uses script-specific encodings for our target setting while maintaining full Unicode coverage through UTF-8 fallbacks, using this framework to model four orthographically diverse languages. Surprisingly, we find that while languages with information-dense characters (Chinese, Korean) significantly benefit from compressive encodings, languages whose characters carry less information individually (Georgian, Tamil) are largely insensitive to encoding choice. In light of these findings, we argue that text encoding should be a language-specific design decision, rather than a universal default.

articles.title: A Lightweight Differentiable Method for Real-Time Skin Rendering and Digitization
articles.content: Inverse rendering for skin typically relies on offline path tracing to estimate physical properties, which fail to map directly to the approximate shaders utilized in interactive applications, such as game engines. We bridge this gap by directly estimating subsurface scattering parameters tailored for real-time rendering pipelines. We introduce a differentiable Screen-Space Subsurface Scattering (SSSS) framework that enables the joint optimization of spatially varying base textures and scattering distances. To account for local variations in skin thickness, we estimate these parameters across distinct facial regions, generating a blended profile map ready for production runtime engines. Our pipeline utilizes a low-cost, single-light, single-view capture setup designed for accessible and practical appearance acquisition. Optimization is driven by a masked loss function targeting regions where subsurface scattering effects are dominant. articles.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
articles.content: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. We introduce UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose. By assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, UGG formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model. This flexible formulation enables the model to learn from diverse, heterogeneous datasets with different subsets of geometric and visual annotations. Furthermore, our generative formulation enables inference-time search over multiple plausible scene hypotheses, using geometric evidence extracted from observed RGB frames to improve geometric prediction without ground truth geometry. We demonstrate UGG's effectiveness over non-unified baselines across camera-controlled video generation, depth estimation, and camera pose prediction, including in challenging sparse observation settings. Code and visualizations are available at https://ugg-model.github.io/

articles.title: Metric-Aligned Group Relative Policy Optimization for Explainable Deepfake Detection
articles.content: Deepfake detectors are commonly evaluated on real/fake classification alone, but real-world applications require explanations of the visual evidence behind each prediction. Joint vision-language models struggle with authenticity assessment, producing "real" narratives for manipulated images. To address this, we propose a decoupled predict-then-explain pipeline as our submission to the ACM Multimedia 2026 Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge, with methods trained and evaluated on the XPlainVerse benchmark. A vision-foundation-model ensemble first classifies the image, then a Qwen3-VL-8B model generates a decision-conditioned explanation of the visual evidence. For fake images, a second Qwen3-VL-8B compresses that text into a short non-expert summary without using the image. We further apply metric-aligned Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to optimize both explainers against the challenge criteria. Under matched conditions, GRPO raises complex BERTScore-F1 from 0.686 to 0.712 and also improves grounding (entity and evidence F1); our submission ranked first on complex BERTScore-F1 and seventh overall.
